hints: Two things change: the shape and the number of shapes. Check them one at a time.
The count goes 1, 2, 3, 4. The shapes go square, triangle, circle, then square again.
The shapes repeat in a cycle of three: ■, ▲, ●. Find which shape comes after ■ in that cycle, and how many there should be.

solution.methodName: Check one change at a time

steps.action: Count the shapes: 1, 2, 3, 4. The count goes up by 1, so the next figure has 5 shapes.
The shapes repeat in a cycle of three: square, triangle, circle, then square again. After ■ comes ▲.
steps.why: The 4th figure goes back to ■, which shows that the shapes repeat. So the 5th figure uses the same shape as the 2nd figure.

steps.action: Put both together: 5 triangles. The answer is ▲▲▲▲▲.

trapNotes.●●●●●: This skips the triangle. The cycle is ■, ▲, ●, so after ■ comes ▲, not ●.
trapNotes.■■■■■: This keeps the square from the last figure. The shape changes every step: ■, ▲, ●, ■, then ▲.
trapNotes.▲▲▲▲: This has the right shape but only 4 triangles. The count goes up by 1 each time, so the next figure has 5.
